newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to float 30-40 pct of Adriatic pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to float 30-40 pct of Adriatic pipeline.

text.p: Croatia said on Monday it would privatise Adriatic crude oil pipeline operator Janaf, valued at 743 million German marks, this year by floating between 30 and 40 percent of the company's shares.
"The privatisation project is going ahead," Economy Minister Davor Stern told Reuters.
He said the government had just mandated Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to lead the issue, planned in some six months from now. The company is 100-percent state-owned.

Its offering would be the third by a Croatian firm after the government floated 30 percent of leading drugs firm Pliva in a bid to privatise it, and Zagrebacka Banka offered 10 percent of its stock in 1996.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has also expressed an interest in taking part in Janaf's sell-off and restructuring.

Before then, the company has to be independently audited and the pipeline itself, linking the Adriatic port of Omisalj with Hungary and Eastern Europe via central Croatia, must also be tested for possible technical faults.
The pipeline now runs at no more than 10-15 percent of its annual 3.5 million tonnes capacity, which industry analysts believe could be doubled with minor investments.
Croatia had hoped to sell 12.5 percent of Janaf's equity at face value, around 90 million marks, to Hungary's MOL last year, but the deal has not been concluded to date.
No privatisation ministry officials were available to comment on a state television report at the week-end that the sale to MOL was imminent.

Since the Adriatic pipeline represents an alternative route for crude shipments to the Russia's Druzhba, the Russian oil industry was also said to be interested in using it for moving crude to the Mediterranean.
